citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 4327. Transfer of custody to local museum upon application (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any nonprofit public, quasi-public, or private association or corporation situated
      within the county where the historical documents are filed, which maintains a museum,
      building or facilities used for the exhibit of historical writings, and which shall
      have adequate facilities for the display and preservation of such documents, may petition
      the court of common pleas of the judicial district embracing the county wherein such
      document or documents are filed for the transfer of the custody of such documents
      for the purpose of their public display.  Upon the filing of any petition, the court shall fix a time for a hearing, and prescribe
      such notice to be given as shall acquaint similar organizations with the filing of
      the petition.  Any other association or corporation meeting the requirements of this subsection
      may intervene in the proceedings with the same effect as if it had been the original
      petitioner, and the court, after hearing, may award custody of any historical document
      or documents to any of the petitioners for such term and upon such conditions as the
      court shall prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Remedy to exist for legal injury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Remedy to exist for legal injury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Remedy to exist for legal injury (2023)
content:
Every person for a legal injury done him in his lands, goods, person, or reputation
   shall have remedy by due course of law, and right and justice administered without
   sale, denial or delay.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Place and form of filing applications for relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Place and form of filing applications for relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Place and form of filing applications for relief (2023)
content:
Applications for relief to any court under section 5101 (relating to remedy to exist
   for legal injury) or under any other provision of law, or documents relating to a
   matter before a magisterial district judge, shall be filed in such office and in such
   form as may be prescribed by general rule or rule of court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Trial by jury

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Trial by jury (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except where the right to trial by jury is enlarged by statute, trial by jury shall
      be as heretofore, and the right thereof shall remain inviolate.  Trial by jury may be waived in the manner prescribed by general rules.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5107. Service of process

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5107. Service of process (2023)
content:
Process may be served or executed on any day of the week except at any church, synagogue,
   meetinghouse or any place of worship.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Transfer of erroneously filed matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Transfer of erroneously filed matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Transfer of erroneously filed matters (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If an appeal or other matter is taken to or brought in a court or magisterial district
      of this Commonwealth which does not have jurisdiction of the appeal or other matter,
      the court or magisterial district judge shall not quash such appeal or dismiss the
      matter, but shall transfer the record thereof to the proper tribunal of this Commonwealth,
      where the appeal or other matter shall be treated as if originally filed in the transferee
      tribunal on the date when the appeal or other matter was first filed in a court or
      magisterial district of this Commonwealth.  A matter which is within the exclusive jurisdiction of a court or magisterial district
      judge of this Commonwealth but which is commenced in any other tribunal of this Commonwealth
      shall be transferred by the other tribunal to the proper court or magisterial district
      of this Commonwealth where it shall be treated as if originally filed in the transferee
      court or magisterial district of this Commonwealth on the date when first filed in
      the other tribunal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 51. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Imprisonment for debt

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Imprisonment for debt (2023)
content:
(a) Constitutional restriction.--The person of a debtor, where there is not strong presumption of fraud, shall not
      be continued in prison after delivering up his estate for the benefit of his creditors
      in such manner as shall be provided or prescribed by law.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Change of venue (2023)
content:
The power to change the venue in civil and criminal cases shall be vested in the courts,
   to be exercised in such manner as shall be provided or prescribed by law.

      or can be found within this Commonwealth of any document issued in connection with

      a letter rogatory issued by a tribunal outside this Commonwealth and shall direct
      the manner of service.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 53. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5328. Proof of official records (2023)
content:
(a) Domestic record.--An official record kept within the United States, or any state, district, commonwealth,
      territory, insular possession thereof, or the Panama Canal Zone, the Trust Territory
      of the Pacific Islands, or an entry therein, when admissible for any purpose, may
      be evidenced by an official publication thereof or by a copy attested by the officer
      having the legal custody of the record, or by his deputy, and accompanied by a certificate
      that the officer has the custody.  The certificate may be made by a judge of a court of record having jurisdiction
      in the governmental unit in which the record is kept, authenticated by the seal of
      the court, or by any public officer having a seal of office and having official duties
      in the governmental unit in which the record is kept, authenticated by the seal of
      his office.

   persons who are subject to the jurisdiction of the tribunals of this Commonwealth
   whether or not the persons to whom the obligations are owed are subject to the jurisdiction
   of the tribunals of this Commonwealth.

      a letter rogatory issued by a tribunal outside this Commonwealth and shall direct
      the manner of service.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Subchapter B. Interstate and International Procedure › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5328. Proof of official records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5328. Proof of official records (2023)
content:
(a) Domestic record.--An official record kept within the United States, or any state, district, commonwealth,
      territory, insular possession thereof, or the Panama Canal Zone, the Trust Territory
      of the Pacific Islands, or an entry therein, when admissible for any purpose, may
      be evidenced by an official publication thereof or by a copy attested by the officer
      having the legal custody of the record, or by his deputy, and accompanied by a certificate
      that the officer has the custody.  The certificate may be made by a judge of a court of record having jurisdiction
      in the governmental unit in which the record is kept, authenticated by the seal of
      the court, or by any public officer having a seal of office and having official duties
      in the governmental unit in which the record is kept, authenticated by the seal of
      his office.

      except as otherwise provided by subsection (b) or by any other provision of this chapter,
      from the time the cause of action accrued, the criminal offense was committed or the
      right of appeal arose.

      matter is filed in an office authorized by section 5103 (relating to transfer of erroneously
      filed matters) or by any other provision of law to receive such document.

content:

      pursuant to this chapter unless, in the case of a civil action or proceeding, a different
      time is provided by this title or another statute or a shorter time which is not manifestly
      unreasonable is prescribed by written agreement.

content:

   may modify or rescind any order within 30 days after its entry, notwithstanding the
   prior termination of any term of court, if no appeal from such order has been taken
   or allowed.

content:

      mesne profits in an action in ejectment filed in response to the notice served under
      section 5527.1 (relating to ten year limitation) or waive the right to such recovery.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 55. Limitation of Time›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5527.3. Reimbursement

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5527.3. Reimbursement (2023)
content:
The defendant in the ejectment action under section 5527.1 (relating to ten year limitation)
   shall have the right to recover such costs for maintenance, improvements, repairs,
   renovations, taxes or other such expenses to benefit the real property as the defendant
   can prove by a preponderance of the evidence that were or should have been the responsibility
   of the record owners, their heirs, successors and assigns.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5528. Fifteen year limitation (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by section 17 (relating to periods of limitation) of
   the act of August 9, 1971 (P.L. 286, No. 74), known as the “Disposition of Abandoned
   and Unclaimed Property Act,”1an action for escheat, or for payment into the State Treasury without escheat, must

   escheated or become escheatable or payable into the State Treasury under any statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 55. Limitation of Time›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 55. Limitation of Time › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If, when a cause of action accrues against a person, he is without this Commonwealth,
      the time within which the action or proceeding must be commenced shall be computed
      from the time he comes into or returns to this Commonwealth.  If, after a cause of action has accrued against a person, he departs from this Commonwealth
      and remains continuously absent therefrom for four months or more, or he resides within
      this Commonwealth under a false name which is unknown to the person entitled to commence
      the action or proceeding, the time of his absence or residence within this Commonwealth
      under such a false name is not a part of the time within which the action or proceeding
      must be commenced.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 55. Limitation of Time › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5534. War
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5534. War (2023)
content:
(a) Cause of action accruing in foreign country.--Where a cause of action, whether originally accrued in favor of a resident or nonresident
      of this Commonwealth, accrued in a foreign country with which the United States or
      any of its allies were then or subsequently at war, or territory then or subsequently
      occupied by the government of such foreign country, the time which elapsed between
      the commencement of the war, or of such occupation, and the termination of hostilities
      with such country, or of such occupation, is not a part of the time within which the
      civil action or proceeding must be commenced, notwithstanding any other provision
      of this subchapter.

      except as otherwise provided by subsection (b) or by any other provision of this chapter,

content:

      unreasonable is prescribed by written agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 55. Limitation of Time›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 55. Limitation of Time › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying (2023)
content:
All actions to recover any or all damages against any person engaged in the practice
   of land surveying occurring as the result of any deficiency, defect, omission, error
   or miscalculation shall be commenced within 12 years from the time the services are
   performed.  Any such action not commenced within this 12-year period shall be forever barred.  The cause of action in such cases shall accrue when the services are performed.  Furthermore, any action shall be commenced within four years from the time that
   such cause of action was discovered, but no later than during this 12-year limitation
   period.  In any event, no action shall be commenced after the 12 years from the time that
   the services are performed.  The term “practice of land surveying” shall be the same as defined under the act of May 23, 1945 (P.L. 913, No. 367)1, known as the Engineer, Land Surveyor and Geologist Registration Law.

content:

   may modify or rescind any order within 30 days after its entry, notwithstanding the
   prior termination of any term of court, if no appeal from such order has been taken
   or allowed.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5538. Landscape architecture (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All actions to recover any or all damages against any person engaged in the practice
      of landscape architecture occurring as the result of any deficiency, defect, omission,
      error or miscalculation shall be commenced within 12 years from the time the services
      are performed.  Any such action not commenced within this 12-year period shall be forever barred.  The cause of action shall accrue upon substantial completion of the project.  Nothing in this section shall be construed as extending the period prescribed by
      the laws of this Commonwealth for the bringing of any action.  The term “practice of landscape architecture” shall be the same as defined in the
      act of January 24, 1966 (1965 P.L. 1527, No. 535), known as the Landscape Architects'
      Registration Law.1

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5572. Time of entry of order (2023)
content:
The date of service of an order of a government unit, which shall be the date of mailing
   if service is by mail, shall be deemed to be the date of entry of the order for the
   purposes of this subchapter.  The date of entry of an order of a court or magisterial district judge may be specified
   by general rules.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5528. Fifteen year limitation (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by section 17 (relating to periods of limitation) of
   the act of August 9, 1971 (P.L. 286, No. 74), known as the “Disposition of Abandoned
   and Unclaimed Property Act,”1an action for escheat, or for payment into the State Treasury without escheat, must
   be commenced within 15 years after the property sought in such action shall have first
   escheated or become escheatable or payable into the State Treasury under any statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5527.3. Reimbursement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5527.3. Reimbursement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5527.3. Reimbursement (2023)
content:
The defendant in the ejectment action under section 5527.1 (relating to ten year limitation)
   shall have the right to recover such costs for maintenance, improvements, repairs,
   renovations, taxes or other such expenses to benefit the real property as the defendant
   can prove by a preponderance of the evidence that were or should have been the responsibility
   of the record owners, their heirs, successors and assigns.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 55. Limitation of Time›Subchapter D. Appeals›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5574. Effect of application for amendment to qualify for interlocutory appeal

Limitation of Time › Subchapter D. Appeals › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5574. Effect of application for amendment to qualify for interlocutory appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5574. Effect of application for amendment to qualify for interlocutory appeal (2023)
content:
If an application is made to a tribunal within 30 days after the entry of an interlocutory
   order not appealable as a matter of right for an amendment of such order to set forth
   expressly the statement specified in section 702(b) (relating to interlocutory appeals
   by permission), the time for filing a petition for permission to appeal from such
   order shall run from the entry of the order denying the amendment or amending the
   order, as the case may be.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5538. Landscape architecture
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5538. Landscape architecture
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5538. Landscape architecture (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All actions to recover any or all damages against any person engaged in the practice
      of landscape architecture occurring as the result of any deficiency, defect, omission,
      error or miscalculation shall be commenced within 12 years from the time the services
      are performed.  Any such action not commenced within this 12-year period shall be forever barred.  The cause of action shall accrue upon substantial completion of the project.  Nothing in this section shall be construed as extending the period prescribed by
      the laws of this Commonwealth for the bringing of any action.  The term “practice of landscape architecture” shall be the same as defined in the
      act of January 24, 1966 (1965 P.L. 1527, No. 535), known as the Landscape Architects'
      Registration Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5537. Land surveying (2023)
content:
All actions to recover any or all damages against any person engaged in the practice
   of land surveying occurring as the result of any deficiency, defect, omission, error
   or miscalculation shall be commenced within 12 years from the time the services are
   performed.  Any such action not commenced within this 12-year period shall be forever barred.  The cause of action in such cases shall accrue when the services are performed.  Furthermore, any action shall be commenced within four years from the time that
   such cause of action was discovered, but no later than during this 12-year limitation
   period.  In any event, no action shall be commenced after the 12 years from the time that
   the services are performed.  The term “practice of land surveying” shall be the same as defined under the act of May 23, 1945 (P.L. 913, No. 367)1, known as the Engineer, Land Surveyor and Geologist Registration Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5532. Absence or concealment (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If, when a cause of action accrues against a person, he is without this Commonwealth,
      the time within which the action or proceeding must be commenced shall be computed
      from the time he comes into or returns to this Commonwealth.  If, after a cause of action has accrued against a person, he departs from this Commonwealth
      and remains continuously absent therefrom for four months or more, or he resides within
      this Commonwealth under a false name which is unknown to the person entitled to commence
      the action or proceeding, the time of his absence or residence within this Commonwealth
      under such a false name is not a part of the time within which the action or proceeding
      must be commenced.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Subchapter B. Civil Actions and Proceedings›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5534. War

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5534. War (2023)
content:
(a) Cause of action accruing in foreign country.--Where a cause of action, whether originally accrued in favor of a resident or nonresident
      of this Commonwealth, accrued in a foreign country with which the United States or
      any of its allies were then or subsequently at war, or territory then or subsequently
      occupied by the government of such foreign country, the time which elapsed between
      the commencement of the war, or of such occupation, and the termination of hostilities
      with such country, or of such occupation, is not a part of the time within which the
      civil action or proceeding must be commenced, notwithstanding any other provision
      of this subchapter.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5747.1. Forfeited undertaking (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a defendant in a criminal prosecution fails to appear for any scheduled court proceeding,
      the defendant's bail may be revoked and notice of revocation shall serve as notice
      of intent to forfeit the bail of the defendant.  The notice or order of revocation shall be served by the office of the clerk to

   law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 58. Forfeiture of Assets›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5805. Forfeiture procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally › Chapter 58. Forfeiture of Assets › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5805. Forfeiture procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5805. Forfeiture procedure (2023)
content:
(a) General procedure.--The proceedings for the forfeiture or condemnation of property, the sale of which
      is provided for in this chapter, shall be in rem, in which the Commonwealth shall
      be the plaintiff and the property the defendant.  A forfeiture petition signed by the Attorney General, deputy attorney general, district
      attorney or assistant district attorney shall be filed in the court of common pleas
      of the judicial district where the property is seized or located, verified by oath
      or affirmation of an officer.  If criminal charges have been filed and a prosecution is pending, the petition shall
      be filed in the same judicial district as the criminal charges in all instances except
      those involving real property.  Each petition relating to real property shall be filed in the jurisdiction where
      the real property is located.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7102. Comparative negligence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7102. Comparative negligence (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In all actions brought to recover damages for negligence resulting in death or injury
      to person or property, the fact that the plaintiff may have been guilty of contributory
      negligence shall not bar a recovery by the plaintiff or his legal representative where
      such negligence was not greater than the causal negligence of the defendant or defendants
      against whom recovery is sought, but any damages sustained by the plaintiff shall
      be diminished in proportion to the amount of negligence attributed to the plaintiff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court (2023)
content:
If the agreement to arbitrate prescribes a method of appointment of arbitrators, the
   prescribed method shall be followed.  In the absence of a prescribed method or if the prescribed method fails or for any
   reason cannot be followed, or when an arbitrator appointed fails to act or is unable
   to act and his successor has not been appointed, the court on application of a party
   shall appoint one or more arbitrators.  An arbitrator so appointed has all the powers of an arbitrator specifically named
   in the agreement.

      described in section 7303 (relating to validity of agreement to arbitrate) and a showing
      that an opposing party refused to arbitrate, the court shall order the parties to
      proceed with arbitration.  If the opposing party denies the existence of an agreement to arbitrate, the court
      shall proceed summarily to determine the issue so raised and shall order the parties
      to proceed with arbitration if it finds for the moving party.  Otherwise, the application shall be denied.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VI. Actions, Proceedings and Other Matters Generally›Chapter 58. Forfeiture of Assets›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 5808. Exceptions

content: (a) Contraband.--Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to apply to the forfeiture of the following:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Settlements and other agreements with hospitalized persons (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An agreement to arbitrate a controversy on a nonjudicial basis shall be conclusively
      presumed to be an agreement to arbitrate pursuant to Subchapter B (relating to common
      law arbitration) unless the agreement to arbitrate is in writing and expressly provides
      for arbitration pursuant to this subchapter or any other similar statute, in which
      case the arbitration shall be governed by this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate (2023)
content:
A written agreement to subject any existing controversy to arbitration or a provision
   in a written agreement to submit to arbitration any controversy thereafter arising
   between the parties is valid, enforceable and irrevocable, save upon such grounds
   as exist at law or in equity relating to the validity, enforceability or revocation
   of any contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators (2023)
content:
The powers of the arbitrators shall be exercised by a majority unless otherwise prescribed
   by the agreement or provided by this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Court and jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Court and jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Court and jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this subchapter shall have, unless the
   context clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Hearing before arbitrators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Hearing before arbitrators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Hearing before arbitrators (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Unless otherwise prescribed by the agreement:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Change of award by arbitrators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Change of award by arbitrators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Change of award by arbitrators (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--On application of a party to the arbitrators, or on submission to the arbitrators
      by the court under such conditions as the court may order if an application to the
      court is pending under section 7313 (relating to confirmation of award by court),
      section 7314 (relating to vacating award by court) or section 7315 (relating to modification
      or correction of award by court), the arbitrators may modify or correct the award
      upon the grounds stated in section 7315(a)(1) and (2), or for the purpose of clarifying
      the award.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Fees and expenses of arbitration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Fees and expenses of arbitration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Fees and expenses of arbitration (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise prescribed in the agreement to arbitrate, the expenses and fees of
   the arbitrators and other expenses (but not including counsel fees) incurred in the
   conduct of the arbitration shall be paid as prescribed in the award.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Representation by attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Representation by attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Representation by attorney (2023)
content:
A party has the right to be represented by an attorney at any proceeding or hearing
   under this subchapter.  A waiver thereof prior to the proceeding or hearing is ineffective.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The arbitrators may issue subpoenas in the form prescribed by general rules for the
      attendance of witnesses and for the production of books, records, documents and other
      evidence.  Subpoenas so issued shall be served and, upon application to the court by a party
      or by the arbitrators, shall be enforced in the manner provided or prescribed by law
      for the service and enforcement of subpoenas in a civil action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Award of arbitrators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Award of arbitrators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Award of arbitrators (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The award of the arbitrators shall be in writing and signed by the arbitrators joining
      in the award.  The arbitrators shall deliver a copy of the award to each party personally or by
      registered or certified mail, or as prescribed in the agreement to arbitrate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Modification or correction of award by court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Modification or correction of award by court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Modification or correction of award by court (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--On application to the court made within 30 days after delivery of a copy of the award
      to the applicant, the court shall modify or correct the award where:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Judgment or decree on award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Judgment or decree on award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Judgment or decree on award (2023)
content:
Upon the granting of an order of court confirming, modifying or correcting an award,
   a judgment or decree shall be entered in conformity with the order.  The judgment or decree may be enforced as any other judgment or decree.  Subject to general rules, costs of any application to the court and of the proceedings
   subsequent thereto, and disbursements may be imposed by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Vacating award by court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Vacating award by court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Vacating award by court (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Confirmation of award by court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Confirmation of award by court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Confirmation of award by court (2023)
content:
On application of a party, the court shall confirm an award, unless within the time
   limits imposed by this subchapter, grounds are urged for vacating or modifying or
   correcting the award, in which case the court shall proceed as provided in section
   7314 (relating to vacating award by court) or section 7315 (relating to modification
   or correction of award by court).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.1. Short title of subchapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.1. Short title of subchapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.1. Short title of subchapter (2023)
content:
This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the Revised Statutory Arbitration
   Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7319. Venue of court proceedings

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7319. Venue of court proceedings (2023)
content: Except as otherwise prescribed by general rules:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Form and service of applications to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Form and service of applications to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Form and service of applications to court (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise prescribed by general rules, an application to the court under
   this subchapter shall be by petition and shall be heard in the manner and upon the
   notice provided or prescribed by law for the making and hearing of petitions in civil
   matters.  Unless the parties otherwise agree, notice of an initial application for an order
   of court shall be served in the manner provided or prescribed by law for the service
   of a writ of summons in a civil action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.3. Notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.3. Notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.3. Notice (2023)
content:
(a) Giving notice.--Except as otherwise provided in this subchapter, a person gives notice to another
      person by taking action that is reasonably necessary to inform the other person in
      ordinary course whether or not the other person acquires knowledge of the notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.2. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.2. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this subchapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.4. When subchapter applies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.4. When subchapter applies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.4. When subchapter applies (2023)
content:
(a) Subsequent agreements.--This subchapter governs an agreement to arbitrate made on or after the effective date
      of this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7320. Appeals from court orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7320. Appeals from court orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7320. Appeals from court orders (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--An appeal may be taken from:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.5. Effect of agreement to arbitrate; nonwaivable provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.5. Effect of agreement to arbitrate; nonwaivable provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.5. Effect of agreement to arbitrate; nonwaivable provisions (2023)
content:
(a) Waiver or variance.--Except as otherwise provided in subsections (b) and (c), a party to an agreement to
      arbitrate or to an arbitration proceeding may waive, or the parties may vary the effect
      of, the requirements of this subchapter to the extent permitted by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.7. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.7. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.7. Validity of agreement to arbitrate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An agreement contained in a record to submit to arbitration any existing or subsequent
      controversy arising between the parties to the agreement is valid, enforceable and
      irrevocable except upon a ground that exists at law or in equity for the revocation
      of a contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.6. Application for judicial relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.6. Application for judicial relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.6. Application for judicial relief (2023)
content:
(a) Procedure.--Except as otherwise provided in section 7321.29 (relating to appeals), an application
      for judicial relief under this subchapter must be made by motion to the court and
      heard in the manner provided by law or rule of court for making and hearing motions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.9. Provisional remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.9. Provisional remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.9. Provisional remedies (2023)
content:
(a) Court.--Before an arbitrator is appointed and is authorized and able to act, the court, upon
      motion of a party to an arbitration proceeding and for good cause shown, may enter
      an order for provisional remedies to protect the effectiveness of the arbitration
      proceeding to the same extent and under the same conditions as if the controversy
      were the subject of a civil action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.8. Motion to compel or stay arbitration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.8. Motion to compel or stay arbitration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.8. Motion to compel or stay arbitration (2023)
content:
(a) Refusal to arbitrate under agreement.--On motion of a person showing an agreement to arbitrate and alleging another person's
      refusal to arbitrate under the agreement:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.12. Appointment of arbitrator; service as a neutral arbitrator
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.12. Appointment of arbitrator; service as a neutral arbitrator
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.12. Appointment of arbitrator; service as a neutral arbitrator (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--If the parties to an agreement to arbitrate agree on a method for appointing an arbitrator,
      that method must be followed unless the method fails.  If the parties have not agreed on a method, the agreed method fails or an arbitrator
      appointed fails or is unable to act and a successor has not been appointed, the court,
      on motion of a party to the arbitration proceeding, shall appoint the arbitrator.  An arbitrator appointed by the court has all the powers of an arbitrator designated
      in the agreement to arbitrate or appointed under the agreed method.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.11. Consolidation of separate arbitration proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.11. Consolidation of separate arbitration proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.11. Consolidation of separate arbitration proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Conditions.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (c), upon motion of a party to an agreement
      to arbitrate or to an arbitration proceeding, the court may order consolidation of
      separate arbitration proceedings as to all or some of the claims if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.10. Initiation of arbitration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.10. Initiation of arbitration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.10. Initiation of arbitration (2023)
content:
(a) Notice.--A person initiates an arbitration proceeding by giving notice in a record to the other
      parties to the agreement to arbitrate in the agreed manner between the parties or,
      in the absence of agreement, by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested
      and obtained, or by service as authorized for the commencement of a civil action.  The notice must describe the nature of the controversy and the remedy sought.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.14. Action by majority
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.14. Action by majority
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.14. Action by majority (2023)
content:
If there is more than one arbitrator, the powers of an arbitrator must be exercised
   by a majority of the arbitrators but all of them shall conduct the hearing under section
   7321.16(c) (relating to arbitration process).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.17. Representation by attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.17. Representation by attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.17. Representation by attorney (2023)
content: A party to an arbitration proceeding may be represented by an attorney.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.19. Judicial enforcement of preaward ruling by arbitrator
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.19. Judicial enforcement of preaward ruling by arbitrator
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.19. Judicial enforcement of preaward ruling by arbitrator (2023)
content:
If an arbitrator makes a preaward ruling in favor of a party to the arbitration proceeding,
   the party may request the arbitrator to incorporate the ruling into an award under
   section 7321.20 (relating to award).  A prevailing party may make a motion to the court for an expedited order to confirm
   the award under section 7321.23 (relating to confirmation of award), in which case
   the court shall summarily decide the motion.  The court shall issue an order to confirm the award unless the court vacates, modifies
   or corrects the award under section 7321.24 (relating to vacating award) or 7321.25
   (relating to modification or correction of award).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.15. Immunity of arbitrator; competency to testify; attorney fees and costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.15. Immunity of arbitrator; competency to testify; attorney fees and costs (2023)
content:
(a) Immunity.--An arbitrator or an arbitration organization acting in that capacity is immune from
      civil liability to the same extent as a judge of a court of this Commonwealth acting
      in a judicial capacity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.20. Award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.20. Award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.20. Award (2023)
content:
(a) Record.--An arbitrator shall make a record of an award.  The record must be signed or otherwise authenticated by an arbitrator who concurs
      with the award.  The arbitrator or the arbitration organization shall give notice of the award, including
      a copy of the award, to each party to the arbitration proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.18. Witnesses; subpoenas; depositions; discovery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.18. Witnesses; subpoenas; depositions; discovery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.18. Witnesses; subpoenas; depositions; discovery (2023)
content:
(a) Subpoenas.--An arbitrator may issue a subpoena for the attendance of a witness and for the production
      of records and other evidence at a hearing and may administer oaths.  A subpoena must be served in the manner for service of subpoenas in a civil action
      and, upon motion to the court by a party to the arbitration proceeding or the arbitrator,
      may be enforced in the manner for enforcement of subpoenas in a civil action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.16. Arbitration process
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.16. Arbitration process
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.16. Arbitration process (2023)
content:
(a) Discretion of arbitrator.--An arbitrator may conduct an arbitration in a manner appropriate for a fair and expeditious
      disposition of the proceeding.  The authority conferred upon the arbitrator includes the power to hold conferences
      with the parties to the arbitration proceeding before the hearing and, among other
      matters, determine the admissibility, relevance, materiality and weight of any evidence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.21. Change of award by arbitrator

content:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.26. Judgment on award; attorney fees and litigation expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.26. Judgment on award; attorney fees and litigation expenses (2023)
content:
(a) Judgment.--Upon granting an order confirming, vacating without directing a rehearing, modifying
      or correcting an award, the court shall enter a judgment in conformity with the order.  The judgment may be recorded, docketed and enforced as any other judgment in a civil
      action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.23. Confirmation of award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.23. Confirmation of award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.23. Confirmation of award (2023)
content:
After a party to an arbitration proceeding receives notice of an award, the party
   must make a motion to the court for an order confirming the award.  The court shall then issue a confirming order unless the award is modified or corrected
   under section 7321.21 (relating to change of award by arbitrator) or 7321.25 (relating
   to modification or correction of award) or is vacated under section 7321.24 (relating
   to vacating award).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.27. Jurisdiction

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter A.1. Revised Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.28. Venue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7321.28. Venue (2023)
content:
A motion under section 7321.6 (relating to application for judicial relief) must be
   made in the court of the county in which the agreement to arbitrate or section 7321.16(f)
   (relating to arbitration process) specifies the arbitration hearing is to be held
   or, if the hearing has been held, in the court of the county in which the hearing
   was held.  Otherwise, the motion may be made in the court of the county in this Commonwealth
   as provided by the Pennsylvania Rules of Civil Procedure.  All subsequent motions must be made in the court hearing the initial motion unless
   the court otherwise directs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter B. Common Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7341. Common law arbitration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter B. Common Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7341. Common law arbitration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7341. Common law arbitration (2023)
content:
The award of an arbitrator in a nonjudicial arbitration which is not subject to Subchapter
   A (relating to statutory arbitration), A.1 (relating to revised statutory arbitration)1or a similar statute regulating nonjudicial arbitration proceedings is binding and
   may not be vacated or modified unless it is clearly shown that a party was denied
   a hearing or that fraud, misconduct, corruption or other irregularity caused the rendition
   of an unjust, inequitable or unconscionable award.

(a) Fairness and expediency.--An arbitrator shall conduct an arbitration in a manner the arbitrator considers appropriate
      for a fair and expeditious disposition of the family law dispute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7381. Temporary order or award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7381. Temporary order or award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7381. Temporary order or award (2023)
content:
(a) Before selection of arbitrator.--Before an arbitrator is selected and able to act, on motion of a party, the court
      may enter a temporary order under 23 Pa.C.S. (relating to domestic relations) and
      the applicable Pennsylvania Rules of Civil Procedure.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7388. Correction or confirmation by court of unconfirmed award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7388. Correction or confirmation by court of unconfirmed award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7388. Correction or confirmation by court of unconfirmed award (2023)
content:
(a) Grounds.--On motion of a party made not later than 30 days after an arbitrator gives notice
      under section 7385(a) (relating to award) or makes a correction under section 7387
      (relating to correction by arbitrator of unconfirmed award), the court shall correct
      the award if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7385. Award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7385. Award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7385. Award (2023)
content:
(a) Manner.--An arbitrator shall make an award in a record, dated and signed by the arbitrator.  The arbitrator shall give notice of the award to each party by a method agreed on
      by the parties or, if the parties have not agreed on a method, under section 7321.3
      (relating to notice).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Short title of subchapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Short title of subchapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Short title of subchapter (2023)
content: This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Uniform Arbitration Act.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Scope of subchapter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An agreement to arbitrate a controversy on a nonjudicial basis shall be conclusively
      presumed to be an agreement to arbitrate pursuant to Subchapter B (relating to common
      law arbitration) unless the agreement to arbitrate is in writing and expressly provides
      for arbitration pursuant to this subchapter or any other similar statute, in which
      case the arbitration shall be governed by this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Validity of agreement to arbitrate (2023)
content:
A written agreement to subject any existing controversy to arbitration or a provision
   in a written agreement to submit to arbitration any controversy thereafter arising
   between the parties is valid, enforceable and irrevocable, save upon such grounds
   as exist at law or in equity relating to the validity, enforceability or revocation
   of any contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7387. Correction by arbitrator of unconfirmed award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7387. Correction by arbitrator of unconfirmed award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7387. Correction by arbitrator of unconfirmed award (2023)
content:
On motion of a party made not later than 20 days after an arbitrator gives notice
   under section 7385(a) (relating to award), the arbitrator may correct the award:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7386. Confirmation of award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7386. Confirmation of award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7386. Confirmation of award (2023)
content:
(a) Motion.--After an arbitrator gives notice under section 7385(a) (relating to award) or makes
      a correction under section 7387 (relating to correction by arbitrator of unconfirmed
      award), a party may move the court for an order confirming the award or, when applicable,
      entry of the divorce decree incorporating the award.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Appointment of arbitrators by court (2023)
content:
If the agreement to arbitrate prescribes a method of appointment of arbitrators, the
   prescribed method shall be followed.  In the absence of a prescribed method or if the prescribed method fails or for any
   reason cannot be followed, or when an arbitrator appointed fails to act or is unable
   to act and his successor has not been appointed, the court on application of a party
   shall appoint one or more arbitrators.  An arbitrator so appointed has all the powers of an arbitrator specifically named
   in the agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7390. Clarification of confirmed award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7390. Clarification of confirmed award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7390. Clarification of confirmed award (2023)
content:
If the meaning or effect of an award confirmed under section 7386 (relating to confirmation
   of award) is in dispute, the parties may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7398. Transitional provision
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7398. Transitional provision
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7398. Transitional provision (2023)
content:
(a) Prospective.--This subchapter applies to arbitration of a family law dispute under an arbitration
      agreement made on or after the effective date of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Action by arbitrators (2023)
content:
The powers of the arbitrators shall be exercised by a majority unless otherwise prescribed
   by the agreement or provided by this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7389. Vacation, amendment or confirmation by court of unconfirmed award

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Court proceedings to compel or stay arbitration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Court proceedings to compel or stay arbitration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Court proceedings to compel or stay arbitration (2023)
content:
(a) Compelling arbitration.--On application to a court to compel arbitration made by a party showing an agreement
      described in section 7303 (relating to validity of agreement to arbitrate) and a showing
      that an opposing party refused to arbitrate, the court shall order the parties to
      proceed with arbitration.  If the opposing party denies the existence of an agreement to arbitrate, the court
      shall proceed summarily to determine the issue so raised and shall order the parties
      to proceed with arbitration if it finds for the moving party.  Otherwise, the application shall be denied.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Chapter 73. Arbitration›Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7391. Judgment on award
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Chapter 73. Arbitration › Subchapter D. Uniform Family Law Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7391. Judgment on award
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7391. Judgment on award (2023)
content:
(a) Entry.--On granting an order confirming, vacating without directing a rehearing or amending
      an award under this subchapter, the court shall enter judgment in conformity with
      the order.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure›Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings›Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration›PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 42 Pa.C.S.A. Judiciary and Judicial Procedure › Part VII. Civil Actions and Proceedings › Subchapter A. Statutory Arbitration › PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 42 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Witnesses, subpoenas, oaths and depositions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The arbitrators may issue subpoenas in the form prescribed by general rules for the
      attendance of witnesses and for the production of books, records, documents and other
      evidence.  Subpoenas so issued shall be served and, upon application to the court by a party
      or by the arbitrators, shall be enforced in the manner provided or prescribed by law
      for the service and enforcement of subpoenas in a civil action.
